newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Turkish navy flexes muscles in north Cyprus.
newsitem.headline: Turkish navy flexes muscles in north Cyprus.

text.p: Three Turkish navy ships docked at a northern Cypriot port on Saturday in a show of strength after a row over the deployment of surface-to-air missiles on the eastern Mediterranean island.
Around 5,000 Turkish Cypriots welcomed the frigate Fatih and the assault boats Gurbet and Dogan when they cruised into Famagusta harbour in the Turkish-occupied north.
A brass band played military marches on the quayside in the bright sunshine.
The visit was a demonstration of solidarity by Turkey with its ethnic kin in Cyprus against Greek Cypriot plans to install Russian-made S-300 missiles on the island.
Ankara has said it will use force if necessary to halt the deployment, due in about 16 months' time.

The missiles' range of 150 km (90 miles) would allow them to hit planes in Turkish airspace but the Cypriot government says the rockets are a defensive measure against Turkey's far greater military might in the region.

"You did not come here to threaten people with war, you came here to bring to the path of common sense those people who are threatening war," Turkish Cypriot Taner Etkin said in a welcoming speech for the ships.
The 2,784-ton German-built Fatih (Conqueror), armed with 127 mm (five-inch) cannon), led the flotilla.
Civilians crowded on to the harbour walls and waved the red-and-white flags of Turkey and the breakaway Turkish Cypriot state in the north of Cyprus that is recognised only by Ankara.
Cyprus has been divided since Turkey invaded in 1974 in response to a coup in Nicosia that was backed by Athens.
"You have demonstrated to the world that Turkey will under no condition stop protecting our security and rights. Come again more often," Etkin said.

Washington says it has calmed down the missile crisis, which has set squabbling NATO allies Turkey and Greece further against each other. But the Cypriot government has refused to scrap the missile deployment and Turkey has warned its threats to use military force are still valid.
